open_points.subject: Flow activation trigger for proven read-only versions (K-08 vs primary action vs M18 source)
open_points.text: K-08: "A read-only flow is activated by the kernel once proven"; Primary actions: "activate a flow | agent or owner asks; the kernel activates a proven read-only version at once"; M18 source: "The kernel, after proof and, for effectful versions, the owner."
open_points.question: When exactly is a proven read-only flow version activated: automatically at successful compose/prove, or only when an explicit activate action is called?
options: Auto-activate immediately when proof succeeds (no separate activate call needed for read-only)
Activate only via the activate action; kernel just waives owner approval for read-only
Both paths allowed (auto on proof, and idempotent activate later)
open_points.default_guess: Activate only via explicit activate action, because State 0 still defines "activate flow" as the action that returns the active version.

open_points.subject: EffectApproval lifecycle when request digest changes before send
open_points.text: Owner decision 18: "Any difference at send, whatever caused it ... asks again." M24 lifecycle defines only `requested` → `approved|refused`, `approved` → `used`, and says unused approvals in ended runs cannot be used; it does not define what happens to an already `approved` record when a changed built request forces asking again while the run is still active.
open_points.question: If a previously approved effect cannot be sent because the built request changed, what model transition occurs for the old approval and what new approval object is created?
options: Keep old approval as `approved` but unusable for this send; create a new `requested` approval for the new request digest
Transition old approval to a terminal superseded/invalid status (new status) and create a new `requested` approval
Mutate the existing approval back to `requested` with updated request digest
open_points.default_guess: Keep the old approval record unchanged (`approved`, never `used`) and create a new approval request record for the changed request.
